title: Okanagan main valley lakes — 1971 chemical limnology (digitised from the Canada–British Columbia Okanagan Basin Agreement, Technical Supplement V)
description:
A verified transcription of Appendix C of the Canada–British Columbia Okanagan Basin Agreement (1974), Technical Supplement V: The Limnology of the Major Okanagan Basin Lakes (compiled by M.E. Pinsent and J.G. Stockner; Office of the Study Director, Penticton, B.C., April 1974).

3,991 depth-resolved observations from six main valley lakes, 21 stations and four 1971 cruises, 1–220 m: nutrients (NO3, TKN, ortho-phosphate, total phosphate, silica) and major anions (bicarbonate, sulphate, chloride, fluoride).

This is the pre-EMS baseline for the Okanagan basin — the provincial in-situ record begins in the 1970s, and the tables in every published copy of the report are scanned images with no OCR text layer for tabular content.

Verification. Nothing is auto-corrected. The transcription is reconciled against the report’s own published summary statistics: Appendix C-3 per-month means reproduce Table 6.4 to 0.0–0.2% for bicarbonate, with sample counts matching exactly for Skaha and Osoyoos across all eight lake-months; Appendix C-1 spring-overturn total phosphorus reproduces Table 6.3 column B (the same Calgary laboratory that analysed the samples) within 1–4%.

Unit warning. Phosphorus is reported as PO4 in Appendix C and Table 6.3, but as P in Table 9.2 — the table that set the basin’s loading criteria. The two differ by a factor of 3.066. Both conventions are carried explicitly as value_as_printed and value_as_P.

Provenance. The underlying report is a joint publication of the Government of Canada and the Province of British Columbia; rights in it rest with the Crown. This record contains a transcription of its tables and the code used to produce and verify that transcription. Transcription errors are the depositor’s, not the 1974 authors’; every value retains the literal source cell so any disputed number can be checked against the page image.
notes: Derived from a Crown publication. See NOTICE.md in the repository: code is MIT-licensed; the transcribed data is offered for reuse with attribution to both the original 1974 report and this transcription.
